raw_response:
I farm the same 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, so I will use all 5 mu for wheat first and then all 5 mu for maize after harvest. I did not start from zero. I will do mostly what has worked for me before, then adjust a little by cost and water. We have well irrigation, so I dare to put a bit more fertilizer because if there is dry weather, I can still push the crop. Wheat cannot be short of base fertilizer, or tillers come weak and the heads are small. Maize cannot be short of nitrogen, or the stalk stays thin and the ears do not fill well. I watch what people around me do, and nobody here wants to save too much on fertilizer and then lose yield. Money is tight because some of the family works off-farm and labor at home is limited, so I will not make the management too complicated. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, do rotary tillage because it is faster and cheaper on 5 mu, irrigate wheat 3 times and maize 2 times with the well, and spray 2 times on each crop unless insect pressure gets bad. I will keep wheat fertilizer a little heavier on phosphorus for rooting and maize heavier on nitrogen for ear filling. That is the safest way for me to hold yield on small land.
